title: Asaaree Ge
description: A wall-mounted diorama of an old coral-stone house courtyard — the veranda front that once lined the lanes of Malé. The study keeps the carved timber doors, the plastered hirigaa wall with its lattice panel, and the shade of a single tree that made the yard livable through the hot part of the day. The blue bench, red cushion and woven mat are modelled from the household objects still found in the old wards.

title: Kalhuvakaru Miskiy
description: A large-scale study of the 1789 coral-stone mosque known as the travelling mosque, raised here with its timber roof frame left exposed so the joinery reads as clearly as the walls. Built during the reign of Sultan Hassan Nooradeen Iskandhar, it is the only structure in the Maldives shaped from kalhu vakaru — ebony lumber — over a carved coral base. The model records the hirigaa masonry, the tiered roof and the way the whole building can be taken apart and moved.

title: Islaamee Marukazu
description: Study of the Islamic Centre and its Grand Friday Mosque — the golden dome that marks the skyline of Malé and the 41-metre minaret beside it. Opened in 1984 and named for Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu al-Auzam, the building follows Malaysian prototypes: a three-storey prayer hall over monumental entrance stairs, framed by lower annexes. The model keeps the chevron-banded minaret, the arched porch and the green-roofed courts that read clearly from the sea.

title: Medhu Ziyaaraiy
description: Study of the central tomb where Abu al-Barakat Yusuf al-Barbari — the scholar said to have brought Islam to the Maldives in 1153 — is buried, across the street from the Friday Mosque. The mausoleum took its present form during the reign of Muhammad Shamsuddeen III in the early 1900s. The model takes in the blue-and-white gateway, the carved timber grille and the slender finial that mark the shrine beside Muliaage.

title: Gaumee Kuthubukhaanaa
description: A lit diorama of the National Library reading room — shelves packed floor to ceiling, a single desk and chair under warm strip lights, drawers and card cabinets built to scale. The library began in 1945 as the State Library, was renamed Majeedhee in 1948 and took its present name, Qaumee Kuthubukhaanaa, in 1982. The model treats the room as a quiet interior: everything is furniture, paper and light.

title: Black Pearl
description: A full-rigged, three-masted sailing ship built plank-on-frame from coconut timber, with hand-turned masts and rigging laid thread by thread. The study follows the tall ships that once worked these waters — square sails set on the fore and main, a spanker aft, the hull carvel-planked and black-hulled above the waterline. Every ratline and deadeye is tied by hand rather than printed.
